citation: Thompson, D.W. (1917) On Growth and Form, Ch. XV, pp. 652-669, Figs. 328
claim_text: Certain hollow structures (e.g. sea-urchin tests diagrammed in Fig. 328, skulls and other shells) take forms explicable as membranes/shells under pressure and tension.
measurable_instance: sea-urchin test meridian profile (axisymmetric approximation of Fig. 328 diagrams)

model.meridian: y(x) = p(x) sqrt(1 - x^2),  p(x) = c0 + c1 x + c2 x^2 + c3 x^3,  x in [-1, 1], half-length = 1
model.cleared_form: p_n r r' + T (r + r') - P r r' = 0
model.pole_equilibrium: p_n = 0 at poles => P R = 2 T
boundary_conditions: axisymmetric solid of revolution about x
poles at x = +/-1 with osculating radius R = p(+/-1)^2
uniform internal pressure P for the spherical null

empirical_claims.C1_axisymmetric_hollow: Test silhouette approximates a solid of revolution (Thompson Fig. 328 cross-sections).
empirical_claims.C2_pressure_tension_closure: Meridian is consistent with Thompson envelope: 2H profile recoverable from pole/equator descriptors.
empirical_claims.C3_near_spherical_family: Echinoid tests cluster near sphere (elongation E = L/B near 1), unlike pointed eggs.
